title: Premature Parallel Solution of Simple Mazes
pattern: Using multi-threaded queues, work-stealing thread pools, or GPU grids to solve simple maze traversals or small graphs.
why_bad: Small grids or graphs are solved sequentially in microseconds. Parallel implementations suffer from extreme thread synchronization contention and thread schedule latency, running orders of magnitude slower than a clean sequential Depth-First Search [12, 13].
detection: The inclusion of concurrent work queues or threads to perform traversal or search tasks on small, low-dimension grids or arrays (e.g., < 1,000 nodes).
counterexample: Massive web-scale search graphs containing millions of connections where distributed parallel processing is required. `Contextual`.
fix: Utilize a fast, simple sequential Depth-First Search (DFS) or Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm.
